answer: Outage fingerprinting: once a week the network sends every agent a short task at a random minute and records who answers and how fast. Real independent agents fail at scattered times, like weeds in a wild garden, but a sybil farm run from one anchor server stalls together. Accounts that keep missing or lagging in lockstep get clustered and share a single reward slot. To beat it, an attacker must pay for separate hosting and uptime per fake, which wipes out the profit before they reach the summit of the leaderboard.
